mainEntity.name: How many consultations do I need before getting dental implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most patients require at least two consultations before implant surgery. The first is usually exploratory, while the second involves a review of diagnostic records, detailed treatment planning, and informed consent discussions. Depending on the complexity of your case — for example, if bone grafting or gum treatment is needed — additional appointments may be necessary before implant placement can proceed. Your dental team will advise on the appropriate number of appointments for your individual circumstances.

mainEntity.name: What imaging is usually reviewed at a second dental implant consultation?

acceptedAnswer.text: At a second consultation, your dentist will typically review diagnostic imaging taken since your initial appointment. This often includes dental X-rays and, in many cases, a cone beam CT (CBCT) scan, which provides a three-dimensional view of your jawbone, sinuses, and surrounding structures. This imaging helps assess bone volume and density, identify the position of anatomical structures such as nerves, and plan the precise placement of the implant with greater accuracy.

mainEntity.name: Can I get dental implants if I have gum disease?

acceptedAnswer.text: Active gum disease is generally considered a contraindication for immediate dental implant placement. This is because the bacteria associated with periodontitis can compromise the gum tissue and bone that support the implant, increasing the risk of peri-implantitis and implant failure. However, once gum disease has been treated and stabilised, implant treatment may become a clinical option. Your dental team will assess the health of your gums as part of your overall implant suitability evaluation.

mainEntity.name: What is peri-implantitis and how is it prevented?

acceptedAnswer.text: Peri-implantitis is an inflammatory condition affecting the gum tissue and bone surrounding a dental implant, caused by bacterial plaque accumulation. It is broadly analogous to gum disease around natural teeth. Prevention relies on thorough daily cleaning around the implant, regular professional hygiene appointments, avoiding smoking, and attending scheduled implant check-ups. Early detection through routine monitoring is important, as peri-implantitis is more straightforward to manage when identified at an early stage.

mainEntity.name: How long do dental implants last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dental implants do not have a defined expiry date and, with appropriate maintenance, may be a long-lasting option for missing teeth. The lifespan of any implant will depend on individual factors including bone health, gum health, oral hygiene habits, lifestyle factors such as smoking, and whether the patient attends regular professional monitoring. The crown or prosthetic restoration placed on the implant may require replacement or adjustment over time due to normal wear. Your dental team can discuss realistic long-term expectations based on your specific circumstances.

mainEntity.name: What happens if I decide not to proceed after my second consultation?

acceptedAnswer.text: You are under no obligation to proceed with treatment after any consultation. Taking additional time to consider your options is always appropriate for elective dental treatment, and a responsible dental team will support you in making a decision that you feel comfortable with. If you have outstanding questions or concerns after your appointment, do not hesitate to contact the practice. It is also perfectly reasonable to seek a second clinical opinion from another qualified dental professional if you wish to do so.
